cards.text: The LORD of Hosts just finished calling out the priests for despising His name (Malachi 1:6-2:9). Now the prophet Malachi speaks about all of them, himself included. He asks two easy questions, the kind where you already know the answer and you don't love where it's headed: "Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us?"

cards.question: Same Father. Same God. So what does Malachi ask why they keep doing to one another?

cards.text: Breaking faith with one another profanes the covenant of their fathers. Then Malachi stops asking and says it straight: Judah has broken faith, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Malachi says Judah has profaned the LORD's beloved sanctuary. How?

answers.text: By marrying the daughter of a foreign god
By bowing down to the idol of a foreign god
By burning incense to the image of a foreign god

cards.text: Malachi doesn't go easy on this one. For the man who does it, he says, may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob everyone who is awake and aware.

cards.question: Malachi says the man who marries the daughter of a foreign god is safe, as long as he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.

cards.text: Then Malachi brings up another thing they do. They cover the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping and groaning.

cards.question: The people of Judah are covering the LORD's altar with weeping and groaning. Why?

answers.text: The LORD no longer receives their offerings gladly
Their enemies have broken down the city walls
The rain has stopped falling on their fields

cards.text: Yet they ask, "Why?" Friend, that's me staring at a flat batch yelling "WHY?!" when I never even turned the oven on.

cards.question: Malachi answers their "Why?" by saying the LORD has been a witness between each of them and the wife of his youth.
They have broken faith with the wife of their youth. Malachi says she is a man's companion and his wife by ___.

cards.text: Malachi asks if the LORD has not made them one, having a portion of the Spirit, and then he asks, "And why one?" He asks AND answers his own question, and I respect that, friend, because up here nobody else is around to answer mine.

cards.question: Malachi says the LORD made husband and wife one, having a portion of the Spirit. The offspring He seeks from them are ___.
Since the LORD seeks godly offspring, Malachi tells the men they are free to send the wives of their youth away.

cards.text: Malachi tells them to guard themselves in their spirit and not break faith with the wife of their youth. Then the LORD, the God of Israel, speaks for Himself, and friend, I turn the mixer OFF for this one.

cards.question: The LORD, the God of Israel, names one thing He hates. What is it?

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts says the man who divorces his wife covers his garment with violence. Then that line again: guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not break faith.

findings.problem: The right answer "Breaking faith" is the passage's own Bible phrase and a two-word answer. The wrong answers "Stealing" and "Mocking" are plain single words. The Bible-sounding answer stands out from the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question reads "what does Malachi ask why they keep doing to one another," and has three problems. The grammar is garbled. "Keep doing" adds repetition that Malachi 2:10 doesn't state: "Why then do we break faith." "They" drops the "we" that card 1 set up ("himself included").

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't click. A batch that never went in a hot oven is raw dough, not a "flat batch," so the cause and the result don't line up the way the joke needs.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Card 9 only tells that the people ask "Why?" and then makes a joke. Nothing before card 10 mentions wives, marriage covenants or the LORD as a witness. That leaves the passage's central answer as a true-or-false coin flip. Card 4 is already a discovery question.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain narration with no reaction, comparison or self-deprecation: cards 3, 5, 7 and 17, and card 1 only lightly. Only cards 9, 12 and 15 have real humor. The passage is serious, but there is room for reactions that don't target the people's sin or the topic of divorce.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
